name: Shared-savings heating optimisation
summary: A provider installs sensors and optimisation software in a building's heating system at no upfront cost to the owner and is paid a share of the measured heating savings.
how_it_makes_money: Provider receives an agreed share of verified heating-energy savings over a contract term. The customer pays no capital expenditure for hardware or software.

software: Web app for customers and operators
sites_assets: Existing building heating systems (multi-family, mixed-use, commercial)
regulation: Building energy regulation and subsidy rules in the target market (check per country)
financing: Provider carries hardware and roll-out cost until savings pay back
channel: Direct to property owners and managers
data: Ongoing metered consumption and sensor data for savings verification

stakeholder_value.customer: Lower heating cost without upfront investment
stakeholder_value.provider: Recurring revenue tied to delivered savings

what_must_be_true: Savings can be measured credibly against an agreed baseline
Achieved savings are large enough to cover provider cost and still leave the customer a gain
The provider can fund hardware and roll-out until payback
Customer accepts a multi-year contract and data access

risks_failure_causes.text: Disagreement on baseline or weather correction makes savings contestable
Low savings in small or already efficient buildings stretch payback beyond what the provider can finance
Owner pays for the system while tenants benefit from lower bills (or the reverse)

cases.note: Sensor-based heating optimisation piloted in multi-family, mixed and commercial buildings; pilots started at 12-15% heating savings. Savings-share model designed with no customer CAPEX. Market outcome of the model to be confirmed.

sources.title: Author's own product work on the Uponor sensor-based heating optimisation pilots
